status_summary: No multilateral Middle East security pact of the kind described was found. Operation Rough Rider against the Houthis ran from 2025-03-15 to a halt announced 2025-05-06 under an Oman-brokered understanding covering US vessels in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab, and on 2025-11-18 the United States and Saudi Arabia signed a Strategic Defense Agreement and the President announced Saudi Arabia's designation as a major non-NATO ally. During the 2026 conflict with Iran, US Central Command enforced a blockade of maritime traffic to and from Iranian ports from 2026-04-13, stating it would not impede navigation to non-Iranian ports, and lifted it on 2026-06-18 under a 60-day memorandum of understanding that provides for safe Hormuz passage without tolls. The National Security Strategy names keeping the Strait of Hormuz open and the Red Sea navigable as core interests but describes no regional pact.

timeline.event: Operation Rough Rider, the US air campaign against the Houthis in Yemen, began, in response to attacks on Red Sea shipping.

The President announced a halt to the US bombing of the Houthis after an Oman-brokered understanding that neither side would attack the other, including US vessels in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The United States and Saudi Arabia signed a Strategic Defense Agreement, per a White House fact sheet, and the President announced treatment of Saudi Arabia as a major non-NATO ally (White House video page; the fact sheet does not mention the designation).

The White House released the National Security Strategy (release date per a law-firm summary; the document cover is dated November 2025), which lists Hormuz and Red Sea navigation among core Middle East interests.

A US blockade of all maritime traffic entering and exiting Iranian ports took effect at 10 a.m. Eastern under a presidential proclamation, with US Central Command stating it would not impede navigation through the Strait of Hormuz for vessels bound to or from non-Iranian ports.
timeline.source: US Central Command statement (via Iran Watch)

timeline.event: US Central Command announced the lifting of the naval blockade of Iranian ports as a 60-day memorandum of understanding with Iran took effect, providing for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz with no tolls and Iranian demining within 30 days.

title: Build a Middle East security pact and protect navigation in the Gulf and Red Sea
uncertainties: The major non-NATO ally announcement rests on one news report, and the Strategic Defense Agreement is confirmed only by a White House fact sheet; no agreement text, State Department notice or Federal Register notice was read. Primary documents that would decide the stage: the text of a multilateral regional security arrangement, if any exists, and State Department records of the Saudi agreement and designation. The blockade start is supported by a US Central Command statement reproduced on a nonproliferation site and a Reuters report; the start date of the 2026 war, the failed talks in Islamabad and US mine-clearance dates appeared only in an online encyclopedia used as a lead and were removed from the record. A blockade of Iranian ports is a coercive measure rather than a freedom of navigation operation; it is counted here only because Central Command stated it would not impede non-Iranian traffic and the settlement restored Hormuz passage. The no-pact finding rests on three searches of news and think-tank material and does not exclude a quiet framework. I2U2, India's role, the Gaza arrangements and North Africa cooperation with France were not researched. The Mecca pact among Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan reported in August 2026 is an opinion piece account and is not a US action. The White House fact sheet of 2025-11-18 confirms signature of the Strategic Defense Agreement (burden-sharing funds, easier operations for US firms) but is a promotional document, not the agreement text, and does not mention the non-NATO ally designation or any regional pact. A White House release of June 2026 on the Iran memorandum was read and contains only commentary, not the memorandum text, so the 60-day term and Hormuz provisions remain secondary (USNI News). No White House presidential-action page for the blockade proclamation was located. The self-published White House list of January 2026 states a Houthi ceasefire restored Red Sea freedom of navigation for US-flagged ships, without dates.
